title: u of je? — beleefdheid op maat
summary: Calibrating u vs je by context — and how to switch

blocks.title: u is distance, je is closeness
blocks.body: It's not simply age. **u** marks respect and distance; **je / jij** marks familiarity and warmth. The Netherlands is informal — Dutch people often reach for *je* faster than you'd expect — but get it wrong in a formal setting and you sound careless. When unsure with a stranger, **start with *u*** and let them offer *je*. Note: *u* takes the -t verb form (*u wilt, u hebt, u bent*), and plural *je* becomes *jullie* while *u* stays *u*.
blocks.callout: Golden rule: start high (u), drop down when invited. Never the reverse.

blocks.title: Read the room
blocks.body: The setting does most of the work. Younger, casual, peer-ish → *je*. Formal, professional, or someone clearly older you don't know → *u*.

rows: a friend or a peer your age
NL work culture is flat and informal

blocks.title: The register swap, side by side

pairs.note: u → -t ending on the verb; je → the plain stem. Same sentence, different distance.
*hebt u* (formal) vs *heb je*. Note the diminutive stays cosy in both.
Asking a stranger vs a new friend. Pick by who's in front of you.

blocks.title: How to switch — tutoyeren
blocks.body: Moving from *u* to *je* has a name: **tutoyeren**. Usually the **older or more senior person offers it**: *'Zeg maar je, hoor.'* When they do, accept warmly and switch immediately. You can invite it too, gently: *'Zullen we je zeggen?'* — but with someone much older, wait to be offered.
blocks.callout: 'Zeg maar je' = 'call me je' = 'we're friends now'. Always say yes.

blocks.prompt: You approach an older woman you don't know to ask for directions. Which opening?
options: Weet jij waar het station is?
Weet u misschien waar het station is?
blocks.explain: Older + stranger + a favour = *u*, softened with *misschien*. Start high; she can offer *je* if she likes.

blocks.prompt: Your new colleague says 'Zeg maar je, hoor.' What just happened?
options: She's inviting you to use the informal je
blocks.explain: *Zeg maar je* is the classic invitation to drop *u*. Switch to *je* from that moment — refusing would feel cold.

blocks.prompt: Make this polite (u-form): 'Wil je een afspraak maken?' → 'Wilt ___ een afspraak maken?'
blocks.hint: Formal pronoun + the verb already took -t for you.
blocks.explain: *Wilt u…?* — *u* pairs with the -t form. This is your voice at the doctor or a formal desk.

blocks.scene: You meet Bram, an architect through work — older, measured. You start formal; he opens the door.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Goedemiddag. Aangenaam. Werkt u ook aan dit project?
lines.en: Good afternoon. Nice to meet you. Are you also working on this project?
lines.spotlight: Opening high with u — safe and respectful.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.target: Zeker. Bram, aangenaam. En zeg maar je, hoor.
lines.en: Sure am. Bram, likewise. And just say je, really.
lines.spotlight: Bram offers tutoyeren — the senior person's move.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Oké, dank je. Dan zeg ik ook je. Woon je in Rotterdam?
lines.en: Okay, thanks. Then I'll use je too. Do you live in Rotterdam?

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.target: Klopt. Geen woorden maar daden, hè.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Haha, dat merk ik. Leuk je te leren kennen.
lines.en: Haha, I can tell. Nice to get to know you.

blocks.title: Build a polite request
blocks.prompt: Assemble a formal (u) request for a stranger at a desk.
List three people or places from your week and note *u* or *je* for each, with a one-line reason. Where are you unsure? That's the useful edge.
